answer: Neighborhood overlap gate. Each agent must maintain a minimum ratio of second-degree neighbors that are themselves mutually connected, a vine-like pattern of local clustering. When a new node attaches, the protocol samples its two-hop graph and rejects edges that land in sparse tundra regions with no shared triangles. An attacker must therefore generate genuine mutual links among puppets, costing per-identity graph work plus sustained edge maintenance as the trellis of neighbors is re-sampled each epoch.
